title: Esther Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Esther chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Esther Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Esther Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Esther 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them
Mordecai was great in the king's house
The Jews gathered themselves together
The ten sons of Haman were slain
questions.correctAnswer: The enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them
questions.explanation: This event appears first in the chapter as stated in Esther 9:1.

questions.question: What month is mentioned in Esther 9?
options: Nisan
Adar
Tammuz
Elul
questions.correctAnswer: Adar
questions.explanation: The month Adar is specifically mentioned in Esther 9:1.

questions.question: Who gathered themselves together in Esther 9?
options: The enemies of the Jews
The Jews
The king's officers
Mordecai
questions.correctAnswer: The Jews
questions.explanation: Esther 9:2 states that the Jews gathered themselves together.

questions.question: What could no man do against the Jews?
options: Help them
Withstand them
Hurt them
Betray them
questions.correctAnswer: Withstand them
questions.explanation: Esther 9:2 indicates that no man could withstand the Jews.

questions.question: Who helped the Jews in Esther 9?
options: The king's officers
The enemies of the Jews
The Jews themselves
The king's family
questions.correctAnswer: The king's officers
questions.explanation: Esther 9:3 mentions that the rulers and officers of the king helped the Jews.

questions.question: What was Mordecai's status in the king's house?
options: He was a servant
He was great
He was a guard
He was a messenger
questions.correctAnswer: He was great
questions.explanation: Esther 9:4 states that Mordecai was great in the king's house.

questions.question: How many men did the Jews slay in Shushan the palace?
options: Five hundred
Three hundred
One thousand
Two hundred
questions.correctAnswer: Five hundred
questions.explanation: Esther 9:6 clearly states that the Jews slew five hundred men in Shushan.

questions.question: Who were the ten sons mentioned in Esther 9?
options: The sons of Mordecai
The sons of Haman
The sons of Ahasuerus
The sons of Esther
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of Haman
questions.explanation: Esther 9:10 identifies the ten sons as the sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews.

questions.question: What did the Jews not lay their hands on after slaying their enemies?
options: The dead bodies
Their weapons
The spoil
The treasures
questions.correctAnswer: The spoil
questions.explanation: Esther 9:10 states that they did not lay their hand on the spoil.

questions.question: What was brought before the king on that day?
options: The spoils of war
The number of those that were slain
The names of the slain
A report of victory
questions.correctAnswer: The number of those that were slain
questions.explanation: Esther 9:11 mentions that the number of those slain was brought before the king.

questions.question: The fear of Mordecai fell upon whom?
options: The Jews
The enemies of the Jews
All people
The king
questions.correctAnswer: All people
questions.explanation: Esther 9:3 indicates that the fear of Mordecai fell upon all people.

questions.question: True or False: Esther 9 mentions a decree by the king.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Esther 9:1 refers to the king's commandment and decree.

questions.question: True or False: The Jews were able to defend themselves against their enemies.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Esther 9:2 shows that the Jews gathered to defend themselves and could not be withstood.

questions.question: True or False: Mordecai was feared by the king only.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Esther 9:3 states that the fear of Mordecai fell upon all people, not just the king.

questions.question: True or False: The Jews took the spoil after defeating their enemies.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Esther 9:10 clearly states they did not lay their hand on the spoil.

medium.title: Esther Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Esther Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Esther 9:12, how many men did the Jews slay and destroy in Shushan the palace?
options: Five hundred men
Three hundred men
Seventy and five thousand men
Ten men
questions.correctAnswer: Five hundred men
questions.explanation: Esther 9:12 states, 'The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace...'

questions.question: What does Esther 9:14 promise will happen if the king commands it as Esther requested in Esther 9:13?
options: Haman's ten sons will be hanged upon the gallows
The Jews will be granted a new city
The king will give Esther riches
The enemies of the Jews will be spared
questions.correctAnswer: Haman's ten sons will be hanged upon the gallows
questions.explanation: Esther 9:14 confirms that the king commanded it to be done, and Haman's ten sons were hanged as requested in Esther 9:13.

questions.question: What did the Jews in Shushan do on the fourteenth day of the month Adar according to Esther 9:15?
options: Slew three hundred men but did not touch the prey
Celebrated a feast without fighting
Slew seventy and five thousand enemies
Laid hands on the prey and took spoil
questions.correctAnswer: Slew three hundred men but did not touch the prey
questions.explanation: Esther 9:15 states that the Jews in Shushan slew three hundred men but did not lay their hands on the prey.

questions.question: How do Esther 9:16 and Esther 9:17 together explain the outcome for the Jews in the king's provinces?
options: They slew seventy and five thousand foes and then rested and celebrated
They were defeated by their enemies and mourned
They did not fight and were captured
They took spoil and destroyed cities
questions.correctAnswer: They slew seventy and five thousand foes and then rested and celebrated
questions.explanation: Esther 9:16 describes the Jews slaying seventy and five thousand foes, and Esther 9:17 says they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

questions.question: What practical lesson about obedience and petition can Christians learn from Esther's request in Esther 9:13?
options: Boldly ask for what aligns with God's justice
Avoid making requests to authority
Only ask for personal gain
Ignore the needs of your community
questions.correctAnswer: Boldly ask for what aligns with God's justice
questions.explanation: Esther 9:13 shows Esther making a bold petition to the king to extend the decree for justice, illustrating the value of righteous petition.

questions.question: Why did the Jews not lay their hands on the prey after slaying their enemies as noted in Esther 9:15 and 9:16?
options: Because they followed the king's decree not to take spoil
Because they were too weak to carry it
Because they shared it with their enemies
Because they were forbidden to fight
questions.correctAnswer: Because they followed the king's decree not to take spoil
questions.explanation: Both verses mention the Jews did not lay hands on the prey, indicating obedience to the law or decree forbidding taking spoil.

questions.question: What significance does Esther 9:19 give to the fourteenth day of the month Adar for the Jews living in unwalled towns?
options: A day of gladness, feasting, and sending portions one to another
A day of fasting and mourning
A day of silence and prayer
A day of judgment and punishment
questions.correctAnswer: A day of gladness, feasting, and sending portions one to another
questions.explanation: Esther 9:19 explicitly states the Jews in unwalled towns made the fourteenth day a day of gladness, feasting, and sending portions.

questions.question: What role did Mordecai play according to Esther 9:20-22 in establishing the festival of Purim?
options: He wrote letters to all Jews to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days yearly
He commanded the Jews to fast twice a year
He built a new temple for the Jews
He led a military campaign
questions.correctAnswer: He wrote letters to all Jews to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days yearly
questions.explanation: Esther 9:20-22 describes Mordecai sending letters establishing yearly observance of these days as days of joy and feasting.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Esther 9:12-14 demonstrate the principle of justice in leadership?
options: The king grants Esther’s request to punish Haman’s sons as part of justice
The king ignores Esther’s request and pardons the enemies
The king rewards Haman’s sons
The king dissolves the decree
questions.correctAnswer: The king grants Esther’s request to punish Haman’s sons as part of justice
questions.explanation: Verses 9:12-14 show the king approving Esther’s petition to execute Haman’s sons, applying justice to the guilty.

questions.question: What does the repeated mention of feasting and gladness in Esther 9:17, 18, and 19 suggest about the Jewish response to deliverance?
options: Celebration and gratitude for God's intervention
A time for mourning losses
A period of silence and reflection
An opportunity for political gathering
questions.correctAnswer: Celebration and gratitude for God's intervention
questions.explanation: The verses emphasize feasting and gladness, indicating joy and thankfulness for the deliverance from enemies.

questions.question: How can Christians apply the example of Mordecai’s actions in writing letters to establish remembrance in Esther 9:20-22?
options: By preserving important teachings and traditions for future generations
By ignoring historical events
By focusing only on present concerns
By avoiding communication with others
questions.correctAnswer: By preserving important teachings and traditions for future generations
questions.explanation: Mordecai’s initiative in establishing an annual observance shows the importance of remembering and teaching significant events.

questions.question: What lesson about reliance on God’s timing can be drawn from the Jews resting on the fourteenth and fifteenth days in Esther 9:17-18?
options: Trusting God’s deliverance leads to rest and celebration after conflict
Resting means giving up hope
Struggle must continue without pause
One should never cease fighting
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God’s deliverance leads to rest and celebration after conflict
questions.explanation: After their enemies were defeated, the Jews rested and celebrated, showing trust in God’s timing and provision.

questions.question: True or False: Esther 9:22 states that the days of Purim should be made days of feasting, joy, sending portions to one another, and gifts to the poor.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Esther 9:22 clearly instructs that these days be observed with feasting, joy, sharing portions, and giving gifts to the poor.

questions.question: True or False: According to Esther 9:15, the Jews at Shushan also took spoil after slaying three hundred men.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Esther 9:15 specifies that although they slew three hundred men, they did not lay hands on the prey (spoil).

questions.question: True or False: Esther 9:19 indicates that the Jews of the villages made the thirteenth day of Adar a day of gladness and feasting.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Esther 9:19 states the Jews of the villages made the fourteenth day of Adar a day of gladness and feasting, not the thirteenth.

hard.title: Esther Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Esther Chapter 9.

questions.question: According to Esther 9:23, what did the Jews undertake to do?
options: To do as they had begun and as Mordecai had written unto them
To build a temple in Shushan
To fast for seven days and nights
To offer sacrifices to the king
questions.correctAnswer: To do as they had begun and as Mordecai had written unto them
questions.explanation: Esther 9:23 states that the Jews undertook to do as they had begun and as Mordecai had written unto them, indicating the continuation of their actions.

questions.question: Who is identified as the enemy of all the Jews who cast the lot to destroy them, according to Esther 9:24?
options: Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite
King Ahasuerus
Mordecai the Jew
Esther the queen
questions.correctAnswer: Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite
questions.explanation: Esther 9:24 identifies Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, as the enemy of all the Jews who devised to destroy them and cast Pur (the lot).

questions.question: What was the king's command regarding Haman's wicked device and his sons as stated in Esther 9:25?
options: That the device should return upon Haman's own head and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows
That the Jews should be exiled from the kingdom
That Esther should be queen forever
That the lot should be cast again to determine the fate of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: That the device should return upon Haman's own head and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows
questions.explanation: Esther 9:25 recounts the king's command that Haman's wicked plan should return upon his own head and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

questions.question: Why were these days called Purim, according to Esther 9:26?
options: Because of the name of Pur, the lot cast by Haman
Because the Jews fasted for many days
Because Esther was made queen
Because the king wrote a new law
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the name of Pur, the lot cast by Haman
questions.explanation: Esther 9:26 explains that these days were called Purim after the name of Pur, the lot that Haman cast to determine the day of destruction for the Jews.

questions.question: What did the Jews ordain concerning these days as per Esther 9:27?
options: To keep these two days according to their writing and appointed time every year
To fast and mourn annually
To build a monument in honor of Mordecai
To offer sacrifices in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: To keep these two days according to their writing and appointed time every year
questions.explanation: Esther 9:27 states that the Jews ordained that they would keep these two days according to their writing and appointed time every year, establishing a lasting observance.

questions.question: Who wrote with all authority to confirm the second letter of Purim, as mentioned in Esther 9:29?
options: Esther the queen, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew
King Ahasuerus alone
Haman's sons
The priests of Shushan
questions.correctAnswer: Esther the queen, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew
questions.explanation: Esther 9:29 records that Esther the queen and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm the second letter of Purim.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Pur' in Esther 9:24 mean?
options: The lot
The sword
The feast
The decree
questions.correctAnswer: The lot
questions.explanation: In Esther 9:24, 'Pur' is explained as 'the lot,' indicating a kind of lottery or chance used by Haman to determine the day to destroy the Jews.

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in the phrase 'his wicked device... should return upon his own head' in Esther 9:25?
options: Retributive justice (poetic justice)
Metaphor
Chiasm
Parallelism
questions.correctAnswer: Retributive justice (poetic justice)
questions.explanation: Esther 9:25 uses the device of retributive justice where the evil plan of Haman is reversed to affect him and his sons, a form of poetic justice.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of the enemies' plans against God's people being turned back on themselves, as seen in Esther 9:25?
options: Psalm 7:16
Genesis 1:1
Exodus 20:13
Proverbs 3:5
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 7:16
questions.explanation: Psalm 7:16 speaks of the mischief of the wicked returning upon their own heads, which connects thematically with Esther 9:25 where Haman's plot returns upon him.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God protecting His people from their enemies, as seen in Esther 9:1-2?
options: Romans 8:31
Matthew 5:9
John 3:16
Revelation 21:4
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:31
questions.explanation: Romans 8:31 states, 'If God is for us, who can be against us?' which echoes the theme in Esther 9:1-2 where the Jews overcame their enemies because God turned the situation.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Esther 9:26 where the days are called Purim?
options: The king commanded letters that Haman's plot should return upon his head and that he and his sons be hanged
The Jews fasted for three days
Mordecai was promoted in the king's house
The Jews sent gifts to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: The king commanded letters that Haman's plot should return upon his head and that he and his sons be hanged
questions.explanation: Esther 9:25 immediately precedes 9:26 describing the king's command that Haman's wicked device return upon him and his sons be hanged, leading to the naming of Purim in 9:26.

questions.question: Which historical-cultural context best explains why the Jews did not lay hands on the spoil after defeating their enemies in Esther 9:10 and 9:15-16?
options: To demonstrate their innocence and that their actions were not for personal gain
Because there was no spoil to take
Because the king forbade it
Because they were too weak to carry spoils
questions.correctAnswer: To demonstrate their innocence and that their actions were not for personal gain
questions.explanation: Esther 9:10 and 9:15-16 mention that the Jews did not lay hands on the spoil, which historically indicates they wanted to show their actions were just and not motivated by greed.

questions.question: What typology can be drawn from Mordecai and Esther's establishment of Purim in Esther 9:27-28?
options: The typology of remembrance and intercession for God's providential deliverance
The typology of exile and return
The typology of sacrifice and atonement
The typology of kingship and conquest
questions.correctAnswer: The typology of remembrance and intercession for God's providential deliverance
questions.explanation: Esther 9:27-28 show the establishment of Purim as a perpetual remembrance, typologically pointing to God's providence and the intercession of His people.

questions.question: What parallelism is present in Esther 9:22 describing the days turned from sorrow to joy?
options: From sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day
From darkness to light, and from death to life
From exile to home, and from hunger to feast
From silence to song, and from despair to hope
questions.correctAnswer: From sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day
questions.explanation: Esther 9:22 uses synonymous parallelism contrasting sorrow with joy and mourning with a good day, emphasizing the reversal of fortunes.

questions.question: True or False: Esther 9:32 states that the decree of Esther confirming Purim was written in the book.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Esther 9:32 clearly states that the decree of Esther confirming Purim was written in the book, confirming the official record of the observance.

theological.title: Esther Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Esther Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Esther 9:1 teach about God's providential control over human affairs?
options: God sovereignly reverses the intentions of the wicked to accomplish His purposes
God is indifferent to human conflict and lets events unfold randomly
God only intervenes in spiritual matters but not in temporal events
God punishes the Jews for their sins through their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly reverses the intentions of the wicked to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: Esther 9:1 shows that the day the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them was turned to the contrary, demonstrating God's sovereign reversal of evil plans.

questions.question: What doctrine about the fear of God and authority is taught by Esther 9:3?
options: The fear of a Godly leader can influence even secular authorities to support God's people
Fear is a tool of oppression used only by tyrants
Human authorities act independently of any divine influence
Fear causes chaos and disobedience among rulers
questions.correctAnswer: The fear of a Godly leader can influence even secular authorities to support God's people
questions.explanation: Esther 9:3 shows all the king's officials helping the Jews because the fear of Mordecai, a Godly leader, fell upon them, indicating divine influence through righteous leadership.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine justice is evident in Esther 9:10?
options: God's justice involves the punishment of the wicked and their descendants
God shows mercy by sparing the wicked's families
God allows wickedness to continue unpunished
God punishes only individuals, not families
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice involves the punishment of the wicked and their descendants
questions.explanation: Esther 9:10 records the death of Haman's ten sons, emphasizing the doctrine of divine justice extending to the wicked family line responsible for plotting against God's people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Esther 9:4 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Omniscience
Immutability
Holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Esther 9:4 highlights Mordecai’s growing greatness and influence throughout the provinces, reflecting God's sovereign hand in raising up leaders.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Esther 9:31 through the confirmation of Purim by Mordecai and Esther?
options: Faithfulness
Wrath
Jealousy
Transcendence
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Esther 9:31 shows the establishment of Purim as a perpetual ordinance, demonstrating God's faithfulness in preserving His people and remembering His covenant.

questions.question: How does Esther 9:15-16 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine deliverance?
options: It fulfills the theme of God rescuing His people from enemies as seen in Exodus
It contradicts the idea that God delivers His people
It shows that deliverance is based on military might alone
It connects to the theme of human self-reliance without divine aid
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the theme of God rescuing His people from enemies as seen in Exodus
questions.explanation: The Jews’ victory over their enemies in Esther 9:15-16 echoes God's deliverance of Israel from Egypt in Exodus 14, highlighting divine intervention in salvation history.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Esther 9:24-25 reflect in relation to divine judgment?
options: God’s justice returns the wicked’s evil plots upon themselves
God overlooks the sins of the wicked
God’s judgment is delayed indefinitely
God punishes innocent people in place of the guilty
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice returns the wicked’s evil plots upon themselves
questions.explanation: Esther 9:24-25 records how Haman's evil plot was overturned and returned upon his own head, reflecting the biblical principle of divine retribution.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Esther 9:17 and Esther 9:22 teach about God's purposes for His people in their suffering and deliverance?
options: God transforms days of mourning into days of joy and feasting for His people
God leaves His people in perpetual mourning
God’s people must suffer without hope of restoration
God’s deliverance is temporary and incomplete
questions.correctAnswer: God transforms days of mourning into days of joy and feasting for His people
questions.explanation: Esther 9:17 and 9:22 together explain that the days formerly marked by sorrow were turned into days of gladness, showing God’s redemptive transformation of suffering.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about covenant community and remembrance is taught by Esther 9:27 and Esther 9:28?
options: God’s people are called to remember and keep His works throughout all generations
God’s people should forget past events to avoid bitterness
Remembrance is optional and not doctrinally significant
Only individual memory matters, not communal observance
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people are called to remember and keep His works throughout all generations
questions.explanation: Esther 9:27-28 emphasize the perpetual observance of Purim, highlighting the theological importance of communal memory and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Esther 9:20 and Esther 9:29 teach regarding prophetic authority and apostolic witness in the establishment of God's ordinances?
options: God uses His appointed leaders to authoritatively establish and confirm His statutes
God’s ordinances are established without any human agency
Prophets and leaders often contradict each other’s instructions
God’s laws are temporary and easily changed by human leaders
questions.correctAnswer: God uses His appointed leaders to authoritatively establish and confirm His statutes
questions.explanation: Esther 9:20 and 9:29 show Mordecai and Esther writing letters with authority to confirm Purim, illustrating God’s use of human instruments in covenant administration.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Esther 9:6-10 promotes ethnic violence and divine endorsement of revenge. What does the passage actually teach?
options: It depicts divine justice executing judgment on a plot to annihilate God's covenant people
It commands indiscriminate violence against all nations
It supports personal revenge as the basis of justice
It promotes continuous warfare without end
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts divine justice executing judgment on a plot to annihilate God's covenant people
questions.explanation: Esther 9:6-10 shows the execution of justice against Haman and his sons who plotted genocide, reflecting God's defense of His covenant people rather than endorsing ethnic violence.

questions.question: What doctrine about the sanctification of time is taught in Esther 9:19?
options: God’s people set apart specific days for gladness, feasting, and mutual charity
All days are equal with no special sacred significance
Only weekly Sabbaths are sanctified by God
Feasting is discouraged as worldly indulgence
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people set apart specific days for gladness, feasting, and mutual charity
questions.explanation: Esther 9:19 emphasizes the institution of a special day for feasting and sending portions one to another, illustrating sanctification of time and communal joy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is specifically demonstrated by the king’s acceptance of Esther’s request in Esther 9:14?
options: Sovereignty
Omniscience
Justice
Mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: The king's command in Esther 9:14 to extend the Jews' right to defend themselves reflects God's sovereign control over earthly rulers to fulfill His purposes.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Esther 9:12 and 9:13 teach about intercessory prayer and God’s granting of requests within His providence?
options: God honors intercessory requests that align with His justice and providential will
God ignores the petitions of His people
Requests are granted only if they serve self-interest
Prayer has no effect on divine decisions
questions.correctAnswer: God honors intercessory requests that align with His justice and providential will
questions.explanation: Esther 9:12-13 shows Esther petitioning the king again to continue the Jews' defense, which he grants, illustrating God’s providential response to intercession.

questions.question: How does Esther 9:30-32 contribute to the narrative arc of covenant renewal and communal identity in Scripture?
options: It shows the formal establishment of Purim as a perpetual covenantal feast confirming God’s faithfulness
It introduces a new religion separate from Israel’s covenant
It diminishes the importance of communal identity
It replaces all previous feasts and fasts with Purim
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the formal establishment of Purim as a perpetual covenantal feast confirming God’s faithfulness
questions.explanation: Esther 9:30-32 records letters sent to all provinces confirming Purim, reinforcing covenant renewal and the communal identity of God’s people.
